title: Print a loop nest
starter:
(* Nest one for loop per (variable, bound), outermost first, with the body innermost.
   Indent two spaces per level. Lines are joined with "\n", no trailing newline. *)
let skeleton (loops : (string * string) list) (body : string) : string =
  body
hints: Build a list of lines and join it with `String.concat "\n"`. The lines are: one `for` header per loop, the body, then one `}` per loop.
Loop number d (0 for the outermost) is indented 2*d spaces; the body is indented 2*n; the closing braces count back down from 2*(n-1) to 0.
`List.mapi` gives you the depth for each header, and `List.init n (fun d -> ...)` builds the closers. `String.make (2 * d) ' '` makes the padding.
explain: A renderer prints loops by recursion or, as here, by counting depth. Getting the closers to mirror the headers is the whole trick; the examples are printed with `String.escaped`, so `\n` stands for a line break.
